title: Refuse a claim or dispatch that cites an unknown or unsettled contract decision
action:
Per D3 (plan.md, Approach, S4): a cell cites contract decisions in the EXISTING cell.decisions field, and a tripwire refuses the dispatch when a cited decision is retired or trigger-waiting. The previous cell built the read this consumes: the settled/unsettled/unknown derivation and the citation resolver, both in verbs/decisions/read.rs. Use them; do not re-derive.

Step 1 - the tripwire's SUBJECT, exactly as the plan defines it. Walk cell.decisions. For each entry, call the citation resolver. An entry that resolves to None is a local D-ID pointing into a CONTEXT.md table, not a store citation: pass over it silently, refuse nothing, warn nothing. For each entry that DOES resolve, read its derived status. Refuse when the status is unknown (the id is not in the active decision set - superseded, redacted, or archived: the plan's resolution of D3's word 'retired') or unsettled (a trigger keyed to it is waiting or due). Refusing on unresolvable entries would refuse 87% of citing cells today and is the single worst thing this cell could do; there is a prohibition for it below.

Step 2 - the claim door. Put the check inside claim_cell_cross_session_ex (verbs/cells/handlers_write.rs, declared :1400), immediately beside the RED_BASE check (:1478-1486). Read that block first and copy its shape exactly: it is pre-store-lock, it calls release_claim before returning, and its own comment states that a refusal there never touches cell status. Yours must be the same - typed, named, and zero-mutation. The cell data at that point is the caller-supplied cell_for_budget (:1407), which is Some on all three doors; reuse that pre-scan rather than re-reading the cell. This one placement covers cells claim, cells claim-next and dispatch prepare --claim, because all three funnel here (:1302, :1385).

Step 3 - the dispatch door. A cell claimed BEFORE its cited decision changed state slips a claim-only tripwire, and D3's letter names the dispatch. Add the same check to prepare's kind == 'cell' arm in verbs/drivers/prepare.rs, where the cell is already loaded, following the existing typed refusal shape there - unmapped_kind_refusal (:56-70) and the claim_ownership refusal (:1016-1030) are the two models; match their {ok:false, type:'refused', reason:..., fix:...} grammar. Both doors must call ONE shared checking function, not two copies of the walk: a rule checked at two points needs one shared read, or the two will disagree.

Step 4 - close the hole that makes the claim door bypassable. normalize_new_cell (verbs/cells/validate.rs:468) preserves any truthy status a caller passes, and validate_new_cell_problems never checks it, so 'bee cells add' with "status":"claimed" produces a cell that never passes the claim door at all. Refuse a new cell whose status is anything but 'open' (absent still defaults to 'open'), with a refusal that names the field and the allowed value. Keep it to cells add; do not touch the claim/verify/cap/block/drop transitions, which handlers_write.rs:435 already guards.

Step 5 - tests. Cell-door cases in verbs/cells/tests.rs, dispatch-door cases in verbs/drivers/tests.rs; judge existing coverage first and author only the gap. From plan.md's test matrix and risk map, the REFUSE cases: a citation resolving to a superseded decision; one whose trigger is waiting; one whose trigger is due; one valid citation alongside an invalid one still refuses. The ALLOW cases matter just as much, because a false refusal stalls every worker: an active decision with no trigger; an active decision whose trigger is resolved; a citation that is a local D-ID like 'D1'; an empty decisions list; a decision carrying no contract tag at all. Plus: every refusal leaves the cell status and the claim store exactly as they were (assert the record, not just the exit code); the same cell refused at the claim door is refused at the dispatch door with the same reason; and 'cells add' with an injected claimed status is refused while an absent status still defaults to open.

Step 6 - sync docs/knowledge/areas/workflow-state/dispatch.md: the tripwire, both doors, the three statuses it refuses on, and - stated plainly - that an entry which does not resolve to a store decision is passed over rather than refused, with the measured reason.

Claiming a cell that cites a decision with a waiting or due trigger is refused the same way

bee cells add refuses a new cell whose status is anything but open, while an absent status still defaults to open

the same shared check in the kind == cell arm, in the existing typed-refusal grammar

prohibitions: Never refuse on a cell.decisions entry that does not resolve to a store decision
No mint trap and no test-writing-cell rule in this cell - that is the next one
No mutation of any kind on a refusal path
No change to the claim/verify/cap/block/drop status transitions
